subcategory: Discover Mana Village, the mythical last Indian hamlet, where ancient legends meet breathtaking Himalayan vistas and the serene Saraswati River.
description: Nestled in the pristine Himalayas of Uttarakhand, Mana Village holds the unique distinction of being the last inhabited village on the Indian side before the Indo-China border. Situated at an altitude of approximately 3,200 meters, just 3 km from the revered Badrinath Temple, its geographical location offers stunning panoramic views of snow-capped peaks and the roaring Alaknanda River. Mana is deeply steeped in Hindu mythology, believed to be the place where the sage Vyasa dictated the Mahabharata to Lord Ganesha, with caves bearing their names serving as ancient relics. Culturally, Mana is home to the indigenous Bhotia community, whose traditional lifestyle and architecture blend seamlessly with the rugged mountain terrain. Visitors can experience their warm hospitality, observe their unique customs, and find local handicrafts, particularly woolens made from sheep and yak wool. The village's serene atmosphere, combined with its profound historical and mythological significance, offers a profound glimpse into India's spiritual and natural heritage.
